title: GREEK NATIONAL SATELLITE SPACE PROJECT - SPACE DOMAIN AWARENESS IN-ORBIT SERVICING (ISOS) PILLAR 2 - PHASE A/B1
description: As part of the Greek National Satellite Space Project - Phase 2, the objective of this activity is the procurement of Phase A/B1 for an In-Orbit Demonstration (IOD) mission aimed at the development and in-space demonstration of a flexible small-satellite platformenabling future In-Space Servicing, Assembly and Manufacturing (ISAM) missions.The mission shall demonstrate autonomous rendezvous,inspection and close-proximity operations (CPO) capabilities in orbit, while supporting the development of European industrial andcommercial capabilities and fostering future operational services.The mission shall address identified user needs and market opportunities with the objective of contributing to the development of future European in-space infrastructure and services. Tenderers shall therefore propose a mission concept that combines technology demonstration objectives with a credible path towards future operational applications.The mission and system development approach shall be based on a modular and scalable architecture, supported byanincremental demonstration strategy with clearly defined primary and extended objectives. The proposed implementation shall prioritise mission success, schedule robustness and affordability, while enabling future capability growth. Primary objectives will focus on demonstrating autonomous rendezvous, inspection and close-proximity operations capabilities, including relative navigation, guidance and control, onboard autonomy, mission operations and payload-carrying capability. Secondary objectives may include extended CPO manoeuvres (V-bar and R-bar approaches), synchronised relative motion demonstrations, technology maturation activities for futureISAM missions, and payload accommodation demonstrations such as advanced sensors or robotics. The implementation of secondary objectives will be subject to available resources and mission opportunities, without compromising the achievement of the primary objectives.

title: UA_AD02 DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT, AND TESTING OF A MEMBRANELESS ELECTROLYZER FOR ENERGY AND LIFE-SUPPORT SYSTEMS AND ISRU TECHNOLOGIES - EXPRO PLUS
description: The availability of oxygen and hydrogen is a key enabling capability for future lunar exploration architectures. These products areexpected to support energy systems, environmental control and life-support systems, and In-Situ Resource Utilisation (ISRU) activities. In the longer term, future exploration missions are expected to increasingly rely on indigenous resources to improve sustainability and reduce logistics requirements. The capability to produce oxygen and hydrogen from locally available resources is therefore considered a strategic enabling technology. The objective of this activity is to design, develop and test a membraneless electrolysertechnology suitable for future space exploration applications, with particular emphasis on the production of oxygen and hydrogen using feedstocks representative of future lunar ISRU scenarios.

description: Objective: The objective of this study is to assess market needs and the delta developments required to adapt current LEO optical communication terminals designsfor use at Very-Low Earth Orbits (VLEO).TargetedImprovements:To enable laser communications from VLEO platforms.Description: Very-Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) orbit is particularly advantageous for satellite communication due to its proximity to the Earth's surface, resulting in reducedlatency, stronger signal and improved link budgets which allow for faster data transmission and smaller terminals potentially lowering the cost andcomplexity of equipment. VLEO satellites are expected to be manufacture in high volume and at much lower cost. In this context the activity will investigatethe market potential as well as the required adaptation of current Laser Communication Terminals (LCTs) for accommodation on future VLEO spacecraftincluding potential aero-stable platforms.The activity shall identify technologies that allow to reduce LCT's size, weight, power and cost (SWaP-C) and to accommodate on current or future VLEOspacecraft where gas-surface interactions increase drag forces and aerodynamic pairs, makingtheir operations significantly different compared to satellitesflying in LEO orbits. The assessment of specific materials in contact with the atmosphere in VLEO are aspects of major importance with respect to theirsuitability for demisability and atomic oxygen surface erosion. Finally, requirements from mass manufacturing and design-to-cost constraints are critical toensure adequate development for VLEO constellations.The project's main tasks shall include:- Identify and analyse the VLEO scenarios/systems expected tobenefit from the use of LCTs (ground-satellite links, optical inter-satellite links).- Identify the critical delta-developments oradaptations from existing LCT designs required for operation in VLEO orbits and for links with Earth andbetween spacecraft.- Providean analysis of delta-development covering optomechanical designs, detectors, pointing acquisition and link maintenance, and communicationtransceiver.The use of appropriate materials for demisability and sustained surface erosion from atomic oxygen are to be considered. Design of mass manufacturingis critical.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs).  For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: S3-SW-16 END-TO-END HELIOSPHERIC PREDICTION PART 1
description: This activity will advance physics-based modelling of the solar corona, solar wind, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and solar energetic particle (SEP) events to improve the prediction of space weather from the Sun to Earth. Using state-of-the-art photospheric magnetic-field observations and in-situ solar-wind measurements as constraints, the activity will enhance the realism and predictive capability of numerical simulations through improved modelling of solar-atmosphere dynamics, solar-wind formation, CME initiation and propagation, and SEP acceleration and transport. The activity will model particle acceleration and release in the lower and middle corona, including flare-associated SEP events and acceleration at CME-driven shocks, together with propagation through evolving coronal and heliospheric magnetic fields. As the first step towards a long-term objective of end-to-end space weather forecasting, the activity will deliver validated software, models, documentation, and demonstrators that significantly strengthen the capability to model and forecast solar drivers of space weather within a common physics-based framework.
